title: Methodus nova et facilis calculum variationum tractandi

deep.reconstruction:
Context (E420, sections 26-30): Euler varies a double integral ∬V dx dy. V depends on x, y, z and the partial derivatives of z up to third order. He treats the variation as a derivative with respect to an auxiliary parameter t, so δz = (dz/dt)dt. The first variation is then dt∬[N z_t + P z_xt + P' z_yt + Q z_xxt + Q' z_xyt + Q'' z_yyt + R z_xxxt + R' z_xxyt + R'' z_xyyt + R''' z_yyyt] dx dy, a sum of ten 'membra'. On this page he integrates members 5 to 10 by parts repeatedly, using the reductions already made for members 2 and 3 on the previous page. In each case all derivatives are moved off δz, leaving a double integral of z_t times a derivative of a coefficient, plus single-integral (boundary) terms.

- Member 5: ∬Q' z_xyt = ∫Q' z_yt dy − ∫z_t Q'_x dx + ∬z_t Q'_xy. This takes one x-integration, then the member-3 rule with P' replaced by Q'_x.
- Member 6: ∬Q'' z_yyt = ∫Q'' z_yt dx − ∫z_t Q''_y dx + ∬z_t Q''_yy.
- Member 7: ∬R z_xxxt = ∫R z_xxt dy − ∫R_x z_xt dy + ∫R_xx z_t dy − ∬z_t R_xxx.
- Members 8, 9 and 10 are treated analogously, ending in −∬z_t R'_xxy, −∬z_t R''_xyy and −∬z_t R'''_yyy.

On the next page the double-integral parts are collected into the field equation N − P_x − P'_y + Q_xx + Q'_xy + Q''_yy − R_xxx − R'_xxy − R''_xyy − R'''_yyy = 0. This is the Euler–Lagrange (Euler–Ostrogradsky) equation for a second-variable functional of third order. The single integrals are boundary terms. In §30 Euler confesses he cannot yet see their meaning or use.
errors: Member 5: the text says 'loco tantum P'' scribi debet (dQ'/dx)'. The rule actually used is the member-3 rule (the coefficient P' of z_yt), so it should read P', not P''. The formula itself is correct.
Member 6: the text says it is reduced 'bis cum secundo collatum'. Both integrations are in y, so the analogy is with the third member (P' z_yt), not the second. The result is correct.
Section number 28 is used twice: once on p.51 and again here. This is a numbering slip in the original edition.

Member 8, as printed: ∫R' z_xyt dy − ∫z_xt R'_x dy + ∫z_t R'_xy dy − ∬z_t R'_xxy. The final double-integral term is correct. A consistent integration path (x, then y, then x) gives ∫R' z_xyt dy − ∫R'_x z_xt dx + ∫R'_xy z_t dy. So the middle boundary term should carry dx, not dy, if it contains z_xt. Alternatively, with an x, x, y path it should be −∫R'_x z_yt dy + ∫R'_xx z_t dx. As printed, the boundary terms are not consistent with any single integration path.

Member 9, as printed: ∫R'' z_xyt dx − ∫z_yt R''_y dx + ∫z_t R''_xy dx. Again the double term is correct. The path y, x, y gives −∫R''_y z_yt dy (dy, not dx) for the middle term. So the middle boundary term has the wrong measure.
These slips are copied into the collected formula on p.53, which repeats the dy/dx assignments. They do not affect the field equation.

Euler writes boundary contributions loosely as single integrals ∫...dy or ∫...dx, without stating limits or the shape of the region. They are only meaningful as integrals over the boundary of a (rectangular) domain. This is the gap he himself acknowledges in §30.

ideas.what: First variation of a double integral whose integrand depends on partial derivatives of the unknown up to third order, reduced by repeated partial integration to a field equation plus boundary terms.
ideas.modern_name: Euler–Lagrange / Euler–Ostrogradsky equation for multiple integrals with higher derivatives (alternating sum of mixed derivatives of ∂V/∂z_α)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lagrange (1760-62) for double integrals (minimal surfaces); Euler E420 (1772) for this general higher-order version; Ostrogradsky (1834/38) and Poisson for the general n-dimensional form with boundary terms
ideas.where_published: E420, Novi Commentarii Acad. Petrop. 16 (1771/72); discussed in histories of the calculus of variations (e.g. Goldstine 1980; Fraser's studies of Euler's and Lagrange's variational work)

ideas.what: Treating the variation as a partial derivative with respect to an auxiliary parameter t (δz = z_t dt).
ideas.modern_name: One-parameter family of variations / Gateaux derivative
ideas.where_published: E420 and the related papers on the calculus of variations of 1771-72

ideas.what: Boundary single-integral terms, which Euler explicitly leaves uninterpreted (§30).
ideas.modern_name: Boundary terms via the divergence/Green theorem; natural boundary conditions
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gauss (1829, capillarity), Poisson, Ostrogradsky (1830s), later Sarrus and Jacobi
ideas.where_published: E420 §30 (open admission); interpretation came later from other authors

missed.claim: The boundary terms for the mixed third-order members (8 and 9) are printed with measures (dy vs dx) inconsistent with any single integration path. The error propagates into the collected formula of §29. I do not know whether the Opera omnia edition annotates this.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only of editorial and historical interest: it shows why Euler found the boundary terms opaque. The field equation is unaffected.

deep.surprise_reason: This is routine integration by parts producing the well-known higher-order Euler–Lagrange equation for double integrals. The unfinished thread (meaning of the boundary terms) is explicitly flagged by Euler and is well known to have been resolved by Gauss, Poisson and Ostrogradsky. The only novelty is minor slips in the boundary terms.
transcription_corrections: Section heading '28.' on this page duplicates the §28 of p.51; it is in the original and is not an OCR error.
In 'vbi loco tantum P'' scribi debet' the printed symbol is hard to read in the scan; mathematically it should be P'.

Fifth member intro: the scan reads 'et loco (dz/dx dt) [scribitur] (d³z/dx dy dt); siue loco (dz/dt) scribendo (ddz/dy dt)'. The first fraction is d d z/dx dt, as transcribed; the transcription is essentially correct.
